text: The system shall refuse what states an agent when it does not state each part that a definition must state.
rationale: OPN-009. DEC-077 divides what states an agent into its parts, and a definition that omits one is not usable. FUN-WC-01 and FUN-ST-01 refuse at admission for the same reason. MET-002 keeps the content of an identity outside this repository, so the system refuses on the parts and not on what they say.

text: The system shall refuse what states an agent when it names a position that is not declared.
rationale: DEC-068 declares a position one time, and an agent that names a position which does not exist holds nothing that a boundary can refuse against. DEC-073 refuses at admission what a lookup settles, and this is a lookup.

text: The system shall refuse what states an agent when the caller that gives it may not confer the position that it names.
rationale: DEC-039 states the positions that a holder may confer. Without this refusal, a caller that may make an agent reaches an authority that its own position refuses, by making an agent that holds it, which is RSK-PL-007.

text: The system shall make an agent that holds a declared position and has a place in the declared hierarchy.
rationale: REQ-PL-016 makes agents. DEC-068 gives the agent one position and DEC-040 gives it a place, and an agent with neither can be neither refused against nor directed. What the caller must give is refused by REQ-AD-001 to REQ-AD-003 and is not restated here.

text: The system shall accept a change to the identity of an agent only from that agent and from the parent of that agent.
rationale: DEC-040 lets a parent change the identity of its child. DEC-077 makes the identity what an agent is for, and the agent is the holder of it. The word only makes this the restriction as well as the act: an earlier text accepted the change without condition and contradicted REQ-AD-018, which refuses the same change when the position of the caller does not admit it. Both gates apply, and the position is not changed by either caller, because what an agent admits is changed by conferral and REQ-AD-020 refuses that.

text: The system shall not give an agent that is retired as the holder of a position.
rationale: DEC-046 ends the holding of a position when an agent is retired. REQ-WC-030 then refuses new work that names that agent, with no second mechanism, and REQ-WC-037 gives the state for the units that are already held.

text: The system shall give what states an agent after the platform stops and starts.
rationale: An agent that the platform forgets when it restarts is not under change control. FUN-WC-02 states the same for a unit of work.

text: The system shall give the identity of an agent and the identity of the position that the agent holds.
rationale: DEC-038 holds an identity at two levels, and a reader that gets one of them does not know how the agent works. MET-002 keeps the content outside this repository and not outside the platform, because DEC-024 gives the data that states what an agent is to this system.

text: The system shall give each earlier configuration of an agent with the time of the change and the caller that made it.
rationale: REQ-PL-016 keeps the history of the configuration of each agent. REQ-AD-005 lets an agent change its own identity, so a change with no author and no time cannot be reviewed.

text: The system shall give what an agent was after that agent is retired.
rationale: DEC-046 retires an agent and does not remove what it was. DEC-022 makes the origin a part of what identifies an assertion, and an assertion of a retired agent stays in life state. DEC-047 does not require that an origin resolves, so this requirement is what makes it resolve while the record is held.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a position that states the part of each body that the position admits, the acts that it admits, the positions that its holder may confer, and the positions whose holders it may retire.
rationale: DEC-029 states the first two, DEC-039 adds the third and DEC-064 adds the fourth. DEC-019 declares the position in one place and each boundary refuses against it, so a declaration that omits a part leaves a boundary with nothing to check: REQ-AD-042 refuses a retirement that the position of the caller does not admit, and it had no declared field to read. REQ-PL-031 is the parent: this row is the act of declaring, and REQ-AD-002 carries the need, because it refuses what states an agent when it names a position that is not declared.

text: The system shall give to a caller the position of an agent and what that position admits.
rationale: INT-PL-09, INT-PL-14, INT-PL-20 and INT-PL-39. DEC-019 declares the position in one place and refuses in many, so each boundary reads the declaration from this system. The four rows name every refusal that this requirement supplies, which MET-021 made expressible: REQ-WC-014, REQ-WC-023, REQ-WC-030, REQ-WC-036, REQ-WC-040 and REQ-WC-045 in Work and Coordination, REQ-ST-017, REQ-ST-018, REQ-ST-032, REQ-ST-034 and REQ-ST-043 in State Custody, and REQ-AU-012 in Authorization. INT-PL-39 adds REQ-AC-006, REQ-AC-007, REQ-AC-008 and REQ-AC-028 in Actuation.

text: The system shall give a position within TBD.
rationale: Every read and every write at every boundary waits for this answer (DEC-019), so this is the one part of the platform that is on the path of all of them. The value depends on the host and on what a boundary needs, and neither is known. REQ-ST-028 carries the same TBD for a query over life state.

text: The system shall give the place of each agent in the declared hierarchy.
rationale: REQ-PL-005 directs work in a declared hierarchy, and DEC-072 arbitrates in it. A tree that a caller cannot read directs nothing.

text: The system shall refuse a change of place from a caller that is not the first common relative of the agent, of the present parent of that agent and of the new parent of that agent.
rationale: DEC-040 admits a change to the hierarchy to the first common relative only. This refusal is by the place of the caller and not by its position, which is why it is here and not in FUN-AD-06.

text: The system shall refuse a change to what states an agent from a caller whose position does not admit the act.
rationale: DEC-019 makes each boundary refuse what a position does not admit, and a change to a definition arrives at this one. REQ-ST-032 and REQ-WC-023 state the same refusal for the declaration of a kind and of a resource.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a position from a caller whose position does not admit the act.
rationale: DEC-039 makes the declaration of a position an act that this boundary refuses. Which callers hold the act is a declaration and not a property of the platform, so this requirement states the refusal and not who is refused.

text: The system shall refuse the conferral of a position that the position of the caller does not state that it may confer.
rationale: DEC-039 states the positions that a holder may confer. REQ-AD-003 refuses the same case when an agent is made; this requirement refuses it when a position is conferred to an agent that exists.

text: The system shall give to an agent the rules for work with the platform.
rationale: Dropped by DEC-077. It gave an agent the rules without saying which, and REQ-AD-054, REQ-AD-055 and REQ-AD-056 now state which. The earlier text: REQ-PL-027. DEC-075 made the rules one of the parts and put them in this system.

text: The system shall give one set of rules to every agent.
rationale: Dropped by DEC-077. DEC-075 made the rules one statement for every agent, and this requirement gave that statement whole to each agent. DEC-077 keeps each rule stated once and gives every agent the rules that bound every caller and gives an agent the rules for the acts that its position admits, which REQ-AD-054, REQ-AD-055 and REQ-AD-056 state. The earlier text: DEC-019 states the failure that a copy for each reader drifts, so a set of rules for each agent, or for each position, is the same failure.

text: The system shall give the set of agents that the platform holds and the position that each agent holds.
rationale: DEC-087 attaches an external client to an agent through Interaction, and a client cannot attach to an agent that it cannot find. DEC-042 states the part of the work body over positions, so a caller that raises work needs the position of an agent and not its name alone.

text: The system shall give only the agents that the position of the caller admits.
rationale: REQ-PL-024 serves to an agent only the part of what the platform holds that its position admits, and DEC-024 puts the data that states what an agent is in this system. A roster that names every agent tells each agent what every other agent is for.

text: The system shall give what states an agent in a form that a runtime outside the platform can use when the platform does not run.
rationale: REQ-PL-021 keeps agents usable when the platform does not run. DEC-043 states what the form carries, and the form carries each part that DEC-077 names, and the rules that it carries are those that REQ-AD-055 and REQ-AD-054 give to that agent. It carries the model that runs the agent, without which nothing outside the platform could run it, which the form states and does not enforce. A form that names a store, a path or a tool of the platform is not usable without it, and how the form avoids that is below this level (MET-005). REQ-ST-021 states the same property of the copy away from the host.

text: The system shall give the position that receives a unit of work that names no agent.
rationale: OPN-030. DEC-076 makes this a flag on one position and not a seventh declaration: no boundary refuses against it, so REQ-AD-011 and REQ-AD-048 to REQ-AD-050 carry its lifecycle with the position register. REQ-WC-012 sends such a unit to one declared agent and nothing declared one. DEC-030 makes the choice of an agent a judgement, so this system gives the declaration and makes no choice. DEC-042 states it over a position and not over an agent, so the agent that receives the work can change with no change here.

text: The system shall confer a position on an agent that exists.
rationale: REQ-PL-016 changes an agent, and the position that an agent holds is a part of what states it (DEC-077). REQ-AD-004 gives a position when the agent is made and REQ-AD-020 refuses a conferral that the caller may not make, so the act itself was refused and accepted and never stated. DEC-068 lets any number of agents hold a position that owns no declared resource, so to confer is not to declare.

text: The system shall refuse a conferral that does not bind each parameter that the position declares.
rationale: RSK-AD-001. DEC-074 binds a parameter when a position is conferred, and a holder with no binding is served the whole of the part that the declaration states. DEC-073 refuses at admission what a lookup settles, and whether a parameter is bound is a lookup. This removes the holder that has no binding. It does not remove the case where the system holds a binding and does not apply it, which no requirement can state.

text: The system shall report when the position that receives a unit of work that names no agent has no holder.
rationale: RSK-AD-004. DEC-046 ends the holding of a position when an agent is retired, and a declared receiver with no holder takes every unit of work that names no agent and gives it to nobody. Whether a position has a holder is a lookup.

text: The system shall not report a change to what states an agent as accepted until it can give that change.
rationale: RSK-AD-008. REQ-PL-016 keeps the history of the configuration of each agent, and a change that is applied before it is recorded leaves a history with a gap. REQ-ST-024 and REQ-WC-025 state the same order for a write and for a unit of work.

text: The system shall report, at an interval of TBD, whether an agent can be used from the form that the system gives for use away from the platform.
rationale: A form that nobody used is not a form that works, and RSK-AD-003 is found only by using it. REQ-AD-026 is the capability; this requirement is how often the platform proves that it still works. The interval depends on what the proof costs on this host, which is not yet known. REQ-ST-025 is the same requirement for the copy away from the host.

text: The system shall report to the caller each change that it refuses and the reason for the refusal.
rationale: A caller that gets silence cannot act. With the reason it can ask an agent whose position admits the act (DEC-026), or state the change in a form that this system admits. REQ-ST-026 and REQ-WC-031 state the same for a write and for a unit of work.

text: The system shall give a copy of what states an agent that is of a state that the system held at one time.
rationale: REQ-PL-022 keeps what states an agent after the loss of the host, and a copy that mixes two states restores an agent that never existed. DEC-020 gives the carriage to External Access and keeps the consistent copy with the system that holds the body, so this requirement gives the copy and names no location (MET-005). INT-PL-13 carries it. REQ-ST-035 states the same property for life state.

text: The system shall restore what states an agent from a copy that it gave.
rationale: A copy that nobody can restore is not a copy. REQ-ST-020 states the same for life state, and RSK-AD-010 is the failure that both answer.

text: The system shall accept a change to the identity of a position.
rationale: DEC-038 holds one identity for each position, and REQ-PL-016 asks that a change common to every agent is made in one place. REQ-AD-005 covers the identity of an agent only, so the shared identity, which exists to be changed in one place, had no act that changes it. The caller is refused by position under REQ-AD-018 and not by place, because a position has no place in the hierarchy (DEC-040).

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a position, and a change to a position, from an agent only.
rationale: REQ-PL-028 accepts a declaration, and a change to a declaration, from an agent only, and DEC-053 gives the reason: to structure a statement of the user into a declaration is a judgement and DEC-030 keeps a judgement out of the platform. REQ-AD-011 accepts the declaration of a position and does not state the writer. DEC-039 makes the declaration of a position an act that a position admits, and this requirement states the writer and not the authority. REQ-AU-002 states the same for a declared class. OPN-050 recorded that REQ-PL-028 had one child while four declaration holders stated nothing.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a position that admits an act on a declared resource which another position already admits.
rationale: DEC-059. Without this refusal, two positions that both admit the acts on one resource restore the failure that ownership removes and nothing observes it. The declared resources and their owners come from Work and Coordination over INT-PL-21. REQ-AD-019 refuses a declaration that the position of the caller does not admit, which is a refusal about the caller. This one is about the position being declared and holds whatever the caller may do.

text: The system shall refuse the conferral of a position that admits an act on a declared resource which another position already admits.
rationale: DEC-059 states the refusal over the declaration and over the conferral. A position can be declared before the resource is, and the owner of a resource can change, so a conferral reaches a position that the declaration boundary passed. REQ-AD-031 refuses a conferral on a different ground and MET-012 keeps them apart. Whether two agents may hold one owning position is settled by DEC-068 and REQ-AD-045, and not by this row.

text: The system shall refuse the retirement of an agent whose position the position of the caller does not admit for retirement.
rationale: DEC-064. REQ-AD-020 refuses a conferral that the position of the caller does not state that it may confer, and DEC-064 mirrors DEC-039 for the opposite act. REQ-PL-005 bounds an agent to the authority that its position gives, and to retire the holder of a position reaches further than that authority when nothing states the bound.

text: The system shall hold, with each agent, the model that runs that agent.
rationale: DEC-065 and DEC-077. REQ-PL-016 keeps the history of the configuration of each agent, and a change of model that the history does not carry is a change nobody can trace a changed answer back to.

text: The system shall hold, with each model that it names, the cost of the use of that model.
rationale: DEC-065. REQ-PL-020 is a constraint that nothing in the model made readable for one agent. A cost that is held only in total tells nobody which agent to change.

text: The system shall refuse the conferral of a position that owns a declared resource on an agent when another agent holds that position.
rationale: DEC-068. REQ-AD-040 refuses a second position over one resource and REQ-AD-041 refuses the conferral of one, and neither reaches a second holder of the one position, which reaches the same effect. OPN-056.

text: The system shall state, in the rules for work with the platform, that a declaration bounds what the platform accepts.
rationale: DEC-069 and REQ-PL-027. The rules must agree with what the platform refuses, and every refusal in the platform is against a declaration (DEC-019). A rule that states the bound stays true when the declaration changes, which a copy of the declaration does not. RSK-AD-007.

text: The system shall not carry the content of a declaration in the rules for work with the platform.
rationale: DEC-069. A copy goes stale (DEC-019), it is paid on every turn that an agent takes, and it invites the agent to judge what a boundary judges. Rule 1 keeps this apart from REQ-AD-046: one row states what the rules say and one row states what they must not carry. RSK-AD-007.

text: The system shall accept a change to what a declared position admits.
rationale: REQ-PL-031. REQ-AD-038 accepts a change to the identity of a position and says nothing about the part of each body and the acts that it admits, which is what REQ-AD-011 declares and what every boundary refuses against (DEC-019).

text: The system shall accept the removal of a declared position.
rationale: REQ-PL-031 and DEC-071. DEC-046 ends the holding of a position when an agent is retired and states that it does not end the position, so a position that no agent holds had no path out of the platform at all.

text: The system shall refuse the removal of a declared position that an agent holds.
rationale: DEC-071. REQ-AD-004 makes an agent hold a declared position, so to remove one that is held leaves an agent that states a position the system does not hold. DEC-046 gives the path: retire the agent, or confer another position, and then remove.

text: The system shall retire an agent.
rationale: REQ-PL-016 makes, changes and retires agents. REQ-AD-004 makes one and REQ-AD-030 confers a position, and retirement appeared only in its consequences, REQ-AD-006 and REQ-AD-010, and in the refusal REQ-AD-042. The act itself was refused and its effects were stated and the act was never stated, which is the defect REQ-AD-030 records for conferral. DEC-046 states what retirement removes.

text: The system shall state, in the rules for work with the platform, where a caller finds the acts that it can do.
rationale: DEC-069 states that Agent Definition says where a caller finds the acts and that Actuation holds them. REQ-AD-046 and REQ-AD-047 state that the rules name the bound and carry no content of a declaration, and neither states where the acts are found, so the one clause that makes the tool reachable was unwritten. REQ-PL-011 makes the interface sufficient for a client that another person wrote, and OPN-061 holds the rest of that flowdown.

text: The system shall give whether any declared position names a given declaration.
rationale: DEC-071 refuses the removal of a declaration that another declaration depends on, and DEC-074 makes a position a predicate over the kind, the subject, the writer, the source and the times of an item, so a position is the declaration that depends. REQ-AD-014 gives the position of one named agent, which answers what that agent admits and cannot answer whether any position at all names a declaration. Without this row REQ-ST-050 and REQ-IN-027 would read every position of every agent and apply the predicate themselves, which puts the shape of a position inside two other compartments. FUN-AD-04 already gives a position to a boundary that refuses; this is that, asked the other way round.

text: The system shall give to an agent the rules for the acts that the position of that agent admits.
rationale: DEC-077. The act ties a rule to a position, because DEC-029 states a position as a part of life state and a set of acts. A rule is stated once, so DEC-019 is met without every agent carrying every rule.

text: The system shall give to every agent the rules that bound every caller.
rationale: DEC-077. REQ-AD-046 and REQ-AD-052 bound every caller whatever its position admits, and RSK-AD-007 rests on every agent receiving them.

text: The system shall not give to an agent a rule for an act that the position of that agent does not admit.
rationale: DEC-077. A rule that an agent cannot use is content that it pays for and reasons over on every turn, which DEC-069 names as a cost to reliability.
